Arcene Journal Dwarf Mountain Holds

Question: If a unit has to test for Restrain or Impetuous and wants to use the Inspiring Presence of a General,which is not inside the unit but has a modified leadership from warband, can the unit use the warband modifier on that generals modified leadership for this test?
Ruling: Yes. The unit uses the modified leadership of the general via Inspiring Presence and does not use the Warband Modifier - the General uses it. The GW FAQ notes that only "a Warband" and thus the unit itself cannot use it.

Question: When do units actually conduct Overrun?
Ruling: Overrun is a pursuit move. The unit has the choice to attempt to restrain or reform, same as for Pursuit or to Overrun and makes then a normal pursuit move bust moves directly forwards. So, the unit moves after break tests.

Question: When a Warband unit makes a leadership test and uses the Inspiring Presence of a warband general (that is not in the unit). How are the multiple warband bonuses applied to this leadership test? Note that this question only adresses the warband modifier and refers to the wording of the Warband special rule.
Ruling: Only the warband modifier of the Generals unit (if he is in a warband unit) is used. If the general is not in a warband unit, then no warband modifier can be claimed.

Question: A unit affected by certain spells (Earthen Ramparts, Miasmic Mirage), formation (marching column) or that has rallied cannot charge or make a charge moves. How does this interact with Random Movers contacting enemies, Counter Charge or Pursuit Into a Fresh Enemy?
Ruling: Since all these count as charging, and therefore as charge  moves for special rules like Frenzy or Furious Charge and Impact Hits, you cannot conduct these  when  under such effects.

Question: When charging a unit in an arc that features an incomplete rank, how are you to make contact with that unit? What happens if you overrun or pursuit into such a unit, but only hit the template or rather footprint?
Ruling:
If charging, Use the footprint of the unit, extending the incomplete rank or file to be complete, and have the charging unit make contact (and maximize contact with) models who would be in those positions.
If Overruning or during a pursuit, you only make contact with such an unit if you hit actual models. In that case, you would conduct your move wheeling to maximise towards the footprint of the unit.

Question: Do fanatics now die when moving through a unit that is entrenched or under the effect of Earthen Ramparts?
Ruling: If the unit is under the effect of Earthen Ramparts but wasn’t charged, they hit the unit since earthen ramparts specifies it only works if charged. Against entrenched or earthen ramparts when charged, the fanatics hit the obstacle and die.

Question: When a character or champion retires from combat, is moved for a challenge, or moves through the ranks, does this count as the unit moving for the purpose of related special rules (such as being 'entrenched')?
Ruling: No. The character (or champion) counts as moving when they retire, but the unit itself does not.

Question: Can I choose for reserves to enter during any player’s turn?
Ruling: No, only on your own turns.

Question: Do modifiers to the To Hit roll apply when using the Seal of Parravon?
Ruling: Yes. The Seal of Parravon refers to a roll of 3 on the To Hit table before modifiers (i.e., the result after consulting the table, not the natural dice roll). Modifiers are applied as normal.

Question: Can the champion of a unit which swapped their shields for another weapon still buy a magical shield? And can the champion chose to wield a separate equipment than the unit (if he wears a mundane/magical weapon?)?
Ruling: Yes, just like how a character doesn't have to buy a generic shield in order to have a magic one. You just need the shield as a possible option to access the magic version. Yes, the champion can use a different weapon option if he has access to.

Question: If Chalice of Dark Rain is active, can a casket of souls use a magical missile? Are wailing dirges affected by it?
Ruling: Only the range of missile weapons is halved´, so the range of Magic Missiles, Wailing Dirge, Breath Weapons and similar rules are not affected (Sky Lantern Bombs), but war machines cannot shoot at all. Since the casket's magic missile is a shooting attack, it cannot be used in such a turn.

Question: Can Sappers use their ability "Dig in!" in every command phase or only in their own?
Ruling: The wording of the special rule "Dig in!" has priority over the general rules for command abilities, thus the special rule can be used in every command phase.

Question: If a unit of skirmishers takes casualties and has no other choice than to remove models in a way that two or more characters that have joined said unit lose coherency with the unit, what happens to the characters?
Ruling: Any model out of coherency, including characters, is removed from play as casualty.

Question: When do you actually conduct accidental contact during a charge? Do you get a charge reaction against it? What happens if you have Fly? And what happens if the original charge target fled?
Ruling:
If wheeling around the obstacle would cause you to do a failed charge, or if the unit is not able to wheel around the obstacle unit at all, you conduct accidental contact during a charge. The charging unit only counts as having redirected prior so it can make contact - you don't get a charge reaction, which only is available after a unit is selected as charge target during a redirect or charge declaration.

A charging unit must endeavour to bring as many models as possible within its front rank into base contact with models in the charged unit. That is the highest priority and the unit must use Fly (X) if needed. You determine if Fly (X) is needed when the unit starts its charge move. If the charging unit with Fly(X)  would make a failed charge and ends on top of the enemy unit, do accidental contact. However, if you fly over/behind the enemy unit, you cannot do accidental contact as it is not the enemy unit, but the missing charge distance that leads to the failed charge.
If the charge target declared flee or is fleeing for any reason, you do not conduct accidental contact during a charge at all, as you have to check for accidental contact during Running Down the Foe. During Running down the Foe, you charge as normally and you never make a failed charge, thus you always try to wheel or move around the obstacle unit. Only if you cannot do that, you will make accidental contact. This means, in most caes, that units with Fly (X) or Skirmishers go over or around obstacle units.
Referenced Rules:
Accidental Contact during a Charge CRB 131
Pursuit into a fresh Enemy CRB 157

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Can an assailment spell be cast from any position in the unit? Does he need to have base contact?
Ruling: The caster has only to be within the fighting rank that is engaged with the unit he wants to target and does not necessarily needs to have base contact to that unit. Note that assailment spells do not lose hits if there is no base contact.

Question: Clarification of the Grail Reliquae.
Ruling: The Grail Reliquae is a single model. It might have the stats of 6 Pilgrims but it's still just a single Heavy Infantry model, which has a Unit Strength of 1. No matter how many wounds it suffers it still has 6 attacks. It is not in Marching Column if it's the only model remaining as single models cannot be in Marching Column. Attacks cannot be directed against the Grail Reliquae - all hits will be assigned to the unit. If a template hits the Grail Reliquae, it results in a normal hit assigned to the unit - note that "risking being hit" for the Grail Reliquae works the same way as for any other model with that base size.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Can stomp attacks in a challenge be also directed towards the unit?
Ruling: No

Question: Due to the GW FAQ about objects being removed from the table, what is an object?
Ruling: Anything that has a real or represented (by template) physical presence on the board that is present for more than a single sub-phase. A unit is a type of object, for example, as is a magical vortex

Question: In the army list for most Armies of Infamy, there will be a text box stating: "Any models that have the option to purchase magic items will have the option to purchase Common or (Faction) magic items). How does this apply to models in the army that are drawn from army books with a different selection of magic items?
Ruling: Models can select magic items from their original army book only (Shaggoths in Wolves of the Sea get only Beastmen items).

Question: When an attack that uses a template (such as Bombardment or an assailment or magic missile that uses a 3" or 5" blast) scatters to be partially off the table, how is this resolved?
Ruling: Template attacks resolved fully even if the template is partially off the table.

Question: If a mounted model casts a spell or uses an ability that affects the caster (such as Mantle of Ghorok), but does not reference other models, does the spell affect the caster's mount (including chariot crew and beasts)?
Ruling: No. A spell or ability that specifies the caster gaining an effect will only affect the wizard itself and not their mount.

Question: Does the "Unity and Harmony" rule affect Cathay units joined by Mercenary characters?
Ruling: No, Jade Warriors & Jade Lancers may only reroll To-Hit rolls of 1 if they are within 3 inches of a mercenary unit. Mercenary characters joined to non-mercenary units do not count.

Question: Can a unit that was drawn from another army list benefit from special rules that mention "friendly <faction> units", for example, a Chaos Spawn in a Beastmen Brayherd Army benefit from a Herdstone?
Ruling: Yes, as it has been picked as part of a Beastmen Brayherds army, although it originates from the Warriors of Chaos rules. This applies for all similar unit entries, which are taken as part of the army list (not as mercenaries or allies except for allied armies of infamies in their corresponding grand army).

Question: Can you see "into" a base of a model or does the base itself block Line of Sight of that Model? Can you aim cannon shots onto the base of a model you see?
Ruling: No, bases fully block line of sight.

Question: Ogdruz Swampcalla and Branchwraith are now the only non‑updated Wizards with the wording "knows spells from the following Lores of Magic” (multiples) instead of “uses spells from … OR …”— does that wording difference create an actual rules distinction?
Ruling: Yes. GW did issue an errata to the other wizards and did not issue an errata to these two. It was not a generalized FAQ, so the wordign remains. Therefore, the exceptions may have access to multiple Lores at the same time.
Referenced Rules:
GW FAQ
Lores of Magic CRB 106

Question: Q: Redress the Ranks requires models to be added (or subtracted) from the left and right side of the unit "as equally as possible." What happens when it is only possible to add models to one side of the unit?
Ruling:
Redress the Ranks can at most add one more model to the left side than the right (or vice versa). If one side is blocked, then a unit can only redress to add a single model to the opposite side.

When removing models, the last models to remove must be the characters, then the command group, always keeping the standard bearer in the front rank and as close to the centre as possible. Command group models removed from the front rank must go to the second rank (and third in case of a single column). Characters removed from the front rank must go to the rear rank. The player choses the position of all models in their respective back ranks. When adding models to the front rank, the opposite order must be followed: first the command group, then the characters, before rank and file models. The position of added models can be chosen by the controlling player, but must respect the positioning rule for the command group and for characters: standard bearer as close to the centre as possible, command group models to either side, characters anywhere in the front rank. Note that characters may be placed among the command group.

Question: Is a unit with Random Movement affected by modifiers applying to their Movement characteristic, such as terrain or spells?
Ruling: Yes. Although models with the Random Movement special rule "do not have a normal Movement characteristic", the result of their dice roll is taken as their Movement characteristic and is affected by modifiers.

Question: The spell Hidden Pathways allows the target to "perform a Quick Turn, even if it would not normally be able to do so." What exactly does this mean?
Ruling: The unit gains Quick Turn and can use it even after marching or if it is not in Open Order formation

Question: If a Character is placed in the rear rank outside of combat because there is no room for them in the front rank, do they count as retired? What happens if there is also no space in the rear rank or he shrinks back into the fighting/front rank? What happens if there is space again for characters that retired because of too many characters or there are only places in the fighting rank left due to shrinking units?
Ruling:
A Character that is not leading from the front is considered retired and cannot confer Inspiring Presence, Hold Your Ground, Aura abilities or similar static benefits unless a rule explicitly states otherwise. Any benefits from spells with the range 'Self' are lost, but spells and abilities that targeted other units or are resolved for global effects remain in effect. Retired models will be counted towards the Units Unit Strength and towards the formation to determine rank bonus, combat order and marching column. They are still considered part of the unit for any check on unit type, model special rule affiliation (unit 'consists entirely' etc.) and target legality (ethereal, unbreakable etc.)

If the character cannot be placed in the rear rank, place him in the closest spot from the rear that is away from a fighting or front rank to retire him. Adjacent characters can be placed behind the rear rank if they retire.

If the unit shrinks down and the character returns by this to the front or fighting rank only because no other position away from a fighting rank is available, he unretires after all casualties are removed, after the initiative step and after any panic checks are resolved, but if this happens in combat he counts as having stepped forward. Outside of combat the usual rules for unretiring characters take place and characters return to the front rank if the formation allows to.

Question: Can you choose when to use the Opal Amulet or are you forced to use it against the first wound?
Ruling: The item gives the bearer a ward save when used, but the player chooses when to activate single use items. Therefore, the Amulet does not have to be used exclusively against the first wound.
Referenced Rules:
High Elves
Single Use Magic Items CRB 337

Question: When a character leaves a unit, how is that character affected by any spells or effects that modify the unit's movement? Do they maintain the unit formation they were in, or always move as a skirmisher?
Ruling: Movement is checked when a character or unit begins their movement. They move as a skirmisher, and move through other models in their unit freely. Any spells or effects (positive or negative) affect the character's movement during the Remaining Moves phase in which the character leaves the unit. This means that if the unit is affected by Miasmic Mirage, the character cannot march, and if the unit is affected by Steed of Shadows, the character may move using Fly (12). If for any reason the character does not follow the Lone Character rules when not in a unit (such as a character on a light chariot), then they must adhere to the normal movement rules for their respective unit type when leaving the unit.

Question: According to GW's FAQ, the Griffon Standard allows its unit to claim a higher rank bonus than normal for its unit type. How exactly does this work?
Ruling: The unit can claim their rank bonus up to the normal maximum for their unit type, but gets +2 instead of +1 for each of these ranks. Infantry with horde have a max of +6 (normally +3), whereas cavalry have a max of +2 (normally +1).

Question: Can the Battle Standard be "claimed as a trophy" in the same way as any other standard (as described p.200), by killing the BSB in combat or running him down?
Ruling: Yes, and the Victory Points obtained are cumulative to the Victory Points granted for slaying the BSB.
Referenced Rules:
Trophies of War CRB 286
Standards CRB 152

Question: How many spells does a Cathay L4 wizard equipped with the Scrolls of Wei-jin and the Learned Feng Shi Bo know?
Ruling: 5 Spells

Question: If a bray-shaman in a Wild Herd army chooses to not use the +1 to cast or dispel from Dark Coven on a spell that they miscast, do friendly wizards within their command range still suffer the effect of that miscast?
Ruling: No. The miscast is shared with friendly wizards only when a bray-shaman chooses to use the +1 from Dark Coven before rolling to cast or dispel.

Turn Order: 2-1 Movement Phase Declare Charges and Charge Reaction
Question: Can you use stand and shoot against a lone character, that would otherwise be protected by the "lone character" rule?
Ruling: Yes, Stand and Shoot does not include targeting

Question: How do I determine the troop type of a unit that includes rank-and-file models with two different troop types?
Ruling: Use the unit type stated in the primary Unit entry (War Beasts / Cavalry for Primal Warhounds for example). However, Rank Bonus and Special Rules that affect models can be applied to individual models (using generals Ld, getting a third rank bonus with horde if the rank consists entirely of Infantry etc).

Question: When a unit fleeing from a charge or a combat flees off the battlefield or is destroyed during its flee move (e.g. due to peril tests, dangerous terrain, fanatics, vortexes,...), what happens to a charging/pursuing unit?
Ruling:
Complete the fleeing unit’s movement, and leave it in place. Then complete charges and pursuits, as if that unit was still fully on the board.

If the fleeing unit is destroyed during the flee move, conduct pursuit and charges towards the position where the last model was removed.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Q: The 1.5 errata states that "Any model that is within a fighting rank and within a number of inches equal to its Movement of the enemy unit can fight." The Random Movement special rule states that "Models with this special rule do not have a normal Movement characteristic. Instead, a dice roll is given (2D6, for example). When a model with this special rule moves, roll the dice to determine its maximum movement." How should this interaction be played?
Ruling:
A) Because the unit does not have a normal movement characteristic when not actively moving, treat the movement value during combat as M (-). This means that models with Random Movement can only make attacks when in base contact with an enemy model.
B) Those units still have a Movement characteristic that deviates from the norm. When a unit with Random Movement has models in a fighting rank but not in base-to-base contact with an enemy models, roll their Random Movement dice when their combat is chosen during step 1.1 of the Combat phase. Use the number rolled as the unit's Movement for this combat phase as the unit's Movement characteristic when determining which models outside of base-to-base can attack. If the unit with Random Movement fights in a 2nd combat during the same combat phase, when that new combat is chosen the unit with Random Movement will roll again to determine this range.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: What Armour Value is used if a model equipped with hand weapon and shield  and the parry spcial rule is engaged in combat and suffers wounds before Step1.1 of his Combat? Can the model use Parry?
Ruling: Use the same Armour Value that would be used if the model were not engaged in combat. The model will use his shield if he has one, but Parry does not apply as his weapon choice has not yet been made for that combat round.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Hatred applies during the first round of combat. If a unit that's already in combat is charged by a new unit, does that count as a new combat for the purpose of Hatred?
Ruling: Only for the charging unit in this example. The first round of combat is relative to each unit, and for Hatred to be used it must be the first round that the unit with Hatred is engaged in that combat.

Question: When dispelling Remains in Play spells during the Conjuration sub-phase, can a dispel attempt be made multiple times (by multiple wizards, for example) against the same spell?
Ruling: No. You may attempt to dispel each Remains in Play spell a single time per Conjuration sub-phase, choosing either a wizard within wizardly dispel range or by making a fated dispel. The same wizard may be chosen to use their wizardly dispel this way against any number of Remains in Play spells.
Referenced Rules: Dispelling Remains in Play Spells CRB 111

Question: If a unit loses models during its movement, e.g. by moving through a fanatic, dangerous terrain, peril tests or a vortex, when are models removed?
Ruling: Remove models right after each damage-dealing source encountered. A reduction in the unit size might affect whether or not it encounters terrain, models or objects behind the first damage-dealing source, and the following wheels might be affected if the unit width is reduced. Charge roll is still affected by terrain based on whether it would be contacted before moving, taking the low dice if the charge path is expected to cross terrain before moving. If the moving unit is a fanatic, he is immediately removed from play and does not move any further if slain.

Question: Are baggage trains considered impassable terrain for the purposes of the crunch rule?
Ruling: No. Baggage trains are not impassible terrain for shooting purposes, including the Crunch rule for cannon fire. They are treated as impassible only for the purpose of moving and positioning units.

Question: When multiple templates would hit a unit in the same shooting sequence (for eample results 2-6 of the miscast table with the dark coven rule or from Sky Lantern bombing), how do you resolve these templates?
Ruling: Resolve the templates at the same time. Every hit is assigned to the model that is actually hit, leading to possibly single models suffering multiple hits. Note for single-wound models, this will possibly cause excess damage, which is then lost. Roll for each model on its own.

Question: Can models in the rear ranks of a formed unit shoot if they are able to draw a Line of Sight? What does "normally" mean in the sentence “Normally, only models in the front rank of a unit can shoot” within [Check Line of Sight]?
Ruling: No. "Normally" means “as a rule”, which applies unless another rule explicitly overrides it (Volley Fire, Vantage Point)

Question: The Sepulchral Animus rules allows a modifier with the following wording: "Once per turn, before making a casting roll, any liche priest within a Mortuary Cult army..." Does that mean the ability can be used once per Priest or only once per army?
Ruling: Once per Priest. The use of "any Liche Priest" indicates that there is no limit on the number of Liche Priests using the ability, as it relates to a unit entry, and not models.

Question: Some special rules use the wording majority of the models (Warband, Immune to Psychology, Frenzy, Run with the Pack as examples). How do these special rules work when there is no majority, and the unit is split half?
Ruling: Unlike Motley Crew, all these rules are optional or buffs to existing rules. For Motley Crew, the rules stop working on a draw, but these rules are full functional. Thus, you need to have more than 50% of the models qualifying for the use of the rule to achieve a majority and make the rule work.

Question: How/When can units draw Line of Sight to points on Hills or in Forests, for example when targeting a point with Cannon Fire?
Ruling: The GW FAQ states that Line of Sight is only obstructed to points behind such terrain features and not in these Terrain Features. For Vantage Points, treat any target point as a unit. Any point on a hill can be seen over models and units, provided they are no closer to the center of the hill as the potential target point.

Question: An ogre loader for a Cathay cannon "joins the crew." What exactly does this mean? How do the gunpowder bombs work?
Ruling:
The ogre loader is considered part of the crew, and thus cannot be hit by enemy shooting (which all goes against the war machine itself). It confers its leadership to the War Machine, aswell as his special rules. The Ogre Loader is not placed on the table as crew, and will just function as other crew members of War Machines.
 In combat, the opponent has to chose wether to attack the Ogre Loader or the Crew as they form two different wound pools with different toughness. For malfunctions, the controlling player can chose which pools loses a wound. Only if both are reduced to 0 wounds, the war machine is destroyed.

When the crew makes ranged attacks using gunpowder bombs, make 4 attacks: one for the ogre, and one for each crew member

Ruling: Yes, the ruling states that a miscast cannot be re-rolled and this applies regardless of the type of re-roll ability.

Question: If a unit defending a Low Linear Obstacle, or counting as defending a Low Linear Obstacle (Dig In, Earthen Ramparts), is charged by an enemy unit that is unable to align, does the defending unit have to align against the enemy unit, hence losing its status?
Ruling: Only for Dug In or Earthen Ramparts, as there is no physical LLO that prevents aligning. With a physical Low Linear Obstacle, the units cannot align to each other, as no base contact to align on was established.

Question: Master Rune of Hesitation says the enemy unit "does not count as having charged for the purpose of choosing which weapons to use or using any special rules it may have." How does this affect weapons that can be used whether charging or not charging, such as cavalry spears or flails?
Ruling: Because the rune only says "for the purpose of choosing," this means that the charging unit cannot choose to use lances. However, it does not negate any benefits those weapons gain when charging (except if they gain special rules, which the rune negates as normal). For example, a flail would grant +2S for charging, but not Armourbane (1).

Question: Are Fanatics units?
Ruling:
Yes, a fanatic is a unit (except for all cases that are explained and listed under their unit entry) as it has a model profile, including characteristics, special rules, equipment etc. This means they work as any other unit, with the following exceptions:
- cannot be charged or have attacks directed against them (with the exception of enemy shooting attacks, against which they count as lone characters) and cannot be targeted by any spells (with the exception of enemy magic missiles), not even by their owner.
- does not engage with other units, but follows the rules for fanatic movement when hitting them.
- do not give away victory points when dying.
- their special rule which allows units to move through them forces units to charge through fanatics towards their charge target.
Note that fanatics being units will force the following interactions:
- They count as unit for the 1" check of give ground, which is not being disabled by the Fanatic Movement rule.
- Fanatics can hit each other (see the COMFAQ entry for units destroyed while moving) and can never leave the board.
- They provide cover and will cause ambushers and units returning from offside the battlefield to keep distance to them.
- They will cause peril tests when units flee through them in addition to the Fanatic Ball & Chain rule.
- They will cause panic in units and will potentially cause units to flee from them if the fanatic is the closest enemy unit.
- Score domination.
Referenced Rules: Ravening Hordes Forces of Evil 26 Fanatics

Question: How is cover determined?
Ruling: Cover is a measure of how obscured LoS is. How much of the "other model or unit" is visible or obscured is determined considering the definition of LoS, including rules that define when models do or don't block Line of Sight (Large Target, Insignificant, Vantage Point). This means, among others, that non-Large models do not provide cover if the shooting or target unit is a Large Target, that models not on a Vantage Point (Hill) do not provide cover if the shooting or target unit is entirely on a Vantage Point (Hill), and that Insignificant models never provide cover. Remember that Large Targets never benefit from cover. Note that for terrain categories that do not have a specific rule for Line of Sight (e.g. buildings, linear obstacles, ruins, battlefield decoration…), Line of Sight has to be determined by checking the actual "true" Line of Sight from the model, if not stated otherwise by the tournament organizer.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: The rule for Transformation of the Dragon states that the new form cannot be placed within 1" of friendly models, within 3" and within 6" of its previous form. The new FAQ states that when the Dragon is in base-to-base contact with enemy models and transforms, it must remain in b2b. As it's impossible to satisfy all of these conditions, how should the rule be played? What happens if there is no room for the new model to be in b2b with the enemy unit?
Ruling:
When a Cathayan Dragon is in combat, their transformation rule ignores the requirements to be further than 1" from friendly models or 3" from enemy models and their base is allowed to overlap their previous form.
If there is no room to place the new model in b2b with the enemy unit due to allied models occupying their full front arc, simply nudge those friendly units aside by the minimum distance necessary to fit the Dragon's new form. However, if there is no space to fit the new Dragon model due to enemy units (even ignoring the 1" rule) or allied units not engaged in the combat, the dragon cannot transform.

Question: How does the Move Through Cover rule apply to units where some models have MTC and other models do not?
Ruling:
The -1M from difficult terrain affects the entire unit, even models not actually in that terrain, but models with the Move through cover special rule will not suffer the -1 Movement penalty.

If a character has joined the unit without Move through cover, he will suffer the penalty (the unit won't) and the unit moves at the modified speed of its slowest model.

In Regard to the higher or lower dice during charges, the unit will always take the lower die if any models do not have the Move Through Cover rule, even if the characters do not actually cross difficult terrain.

Question: Some spells and abilities ask a model to take an Initiative test, such as Terrors Below or Durthu's Wrath. How do temporary modifiers, such as spells, charging, or weapon special rules, affect these? Similarly, what initiative value is used when making an attack with a spell or weapon other than the one chosen to fight with during step 1.1 of combat?
Ruling: A model's initiative for attacking, casting an assailment, or making a test always uses its current (modified) value. If tests are made in the Combat Phase, this includes the Charging Units Initiative bonus, even if the test is made out of combat in a turn that unit charges or counts as having charged. However, special rules from / on weapons like Strikes Last or Always Strikes First apply only to attacks made with those weapons - ignore these rules for all other purposes, including attacks made with different weapons or by different models on a combined profile. In the case of Spectral Doppelganger, attacks with a weapon with Strike First are still resolved on the same initiative as the spell is cast.
